main_text.head: SECT. III. De vocalibus aliisque notis.
main_text.p: Vocales habent tres, eafdem scil. quas Arabes.
main_text.l: Fatha [Arabic fatha sign] a vel e.
Damma [Arabic damma sign] o vel u.
Kefra [Arabic kesra sign] i, Sæpè e brevisimum.
main_text.p: Tres consonæ quiescentes, scil. [Arabic ا و ي letters] naturam vocalium præcedentium induunt, & in unam longam coalescunt, scil. [Arabic alif] cum Fatha, [Arabic] cum Damma, & [Arabic] cum Kefra, ut suprà diximus in Arabicis, quò lectorem remittimus. Hoc tamen addendum quod Fatha cum [Arabic alif], sequente [Arabic] vel [Arabic waw], tanquam o obscurum effertur, ut [Arabic word: adamion] adamion Homines; Idemque valet interdum cùm [Arabic alif] initio dictionis habet hanc notam (~), quæ Medda dicitur, Fatha

page.notes: Arabic script inline is rendered as placeholders where the letters are not reproduced exactly. The Arabic letters and vowel signs in the vowel table, the consonant list (ي ۅ ا), the inline words and the Arabic word "adamion" (أدمیون) are not transcribed letter by letter; the printed Arabic forms should be checked against the scan. The catchword "Fatha" at the foot is the start of the next word and is printed as "Fatha" with a following Arabic-style sign. The "Medda" note mark is a printed tilde within parentheses.
